article.title: How Many Units Are in a Bottle of Wine? UK Guide
article.body:
How Many Units Are in a Bottle of Wine? UK Guide

A 75cl bottle of wine at 12% ABV contains 9 UK units, and one at 14% contains 10.5. To work it out, multiply the ABV by the volume in millilitres and divide by 1,000. Drinks House 247 suggests checking the ABV on the label, because wine ranges from about 11% to 15%.

Units are the UK's way of measuring how much pure alcohol is in a drink. They are useful because they cut through the confusion of different glass sizes and strengths: a large glass of a strong red and a small glass of a light white look similar, but can contain very different amounts of alcohol.

What is a UK unit of alcohol?

One UK unit is 10ml, or 8g, of pure alcohol. That is roughly the amount an average adult's body can process in about an hour, although this varies considerably from person to person. A unit is the same regardless of the drink it comes in: 25ml of a 40% spirit, half a pint of 3.5% beer and a little under 85ml of a 12% wine each contain about one unit.

How do you calculate units?

Multiply the strength of the drink (its ABV, as a percentage) by the volume in millilitres, then divide by 1,000.

Units = ABV × volume in ml ÷ 1,000

For a 75cl bottle of 13% wine: 13 × 750 ÷ 1,000 = 9.75 units. For a 175ml glass of the same wine: 13 × 175 ÷ 1,000 = 2.3 units.

Units by strength and serving size

ABV Bottle (750ml) Small glass (125ml) Medium glass (175ml) Large glass (250ml)
11%8.31.41.92.8
12%9.01.52.13.0
13%9.81.62.33.3
14%10.51.82.53.5
15%11.31.92.63.8

Figures are rounded to one decimal place. A large 250ml glass is a third of a bottle, which is why it adds up so quickly.

How does wine compare with other drinks?

Because units measure alcohol rather than volume, they make different drinks easy to compare. A pint of 4% beer contains about 2.3 units, the same as a medium 175ml glass of 13% wine. A single 25ml measure of a 40% spirit contains 1 unit, and a 125ml glass of 12% champagne contains 1.5. A bottle of 13% wine shared between two people is roughly the same as each person drinking two pints of 4% beer.

How strong is wine, typically?

Most wine sits between 11% and 15% ABV, and the strength depends mainly on how ripe the grapes were:

  • Lighter whites, such as German Riesling or Vinho Verde, can be 8% to 11.5%.
  • Champagne and most sparkling wine is usually around 12% to 12.5%.
  • Many everyday reds and whites fall between 12.5% and 13.5%.
  • Warm-climate reds, such as Zinfandel, Amarone or Barossa Shiraz, often reach 14.5% to 15% or more.
  • Fortified wines such as port are around 19% to 20%, so a 75cl bottle contains about 15 units, and a 50ml glass about one unit.

The ABV is always printed on the label, and many UK labels also show the number of units in the bottle and in a standard glass.

What about bigger bottles?

A magnum holds 1.5 litres, twice a standard bottle, so a 12% magnum contains 18 units. A half bottle of 37.5cl at 12% contains 4.5 units. The formula works for any size.

What are the UK guidelines?

The UK Chief Medical Officers' guideline for both men and women is not to drink more than 14 units a week on a regular basis. If you do drink that much, it is best spread over three or more days, with several drink-free days each week. Fourteen units is about six medium 175ml glasses of 13% wine, or a little under one and a half bottles of 13% wine across a week.

Units are also a helpful way to keep track at a party or dinner, where top-ups make it easy to lose count. Knowing that a bottle of 13.5% red shared between two people is about five units each makes it easier to pace an evening.

What about driving?

There is no reliable way to use units to work out whether you are under the drink-drive limit. Alcohol affects everyone differently, depending on weight, sex, age, metabolism, food and more. The only safe approach is not to drink at all if you are driving, and to remember that alcohol can still be in your system the following morning.

Frequently asked questions

How many units are in a bottle of wine?

A 75cl bottle at 12% ABV contains 9 units; at 13% it contains 9.75, and at 14% it contains 10.5. Multiply the ABV by 750 and divide by 1,000 for any bottle.

How many units are in a glass of wine?

At 13% ABV, a 125ml glass contains about 1.6 units, a 175ml glass about 2.3 units and a 250ml glass about 3.3 units.

How do you calculate units of alcohol?

Multiply the ABV by the volume in millilitres and divide by 1,000. For example, 175ml of 12% wine is 12 × 175 ÷ 1,000, which is 2.1 units.

What is the UK weekly alcohol guideline?

The UK Chief Medical Officers advise not regularly drinking more than 14 units a week, spread over three or more days, with several drink-free days.
